schema.description: Heuristic mapping of A2WF v1.1 declarations to EU-relevant regulatory anchors. Used by the A2WF EU Governance Readiness Checker tool to produce educational guidance. NOT legal advice. The mapping reflects publicly-known regulation text as of 2026-05; a real legal review is the publisher's own responsibility.
schema.disclaimer: This file describes WHERE in a published A2WF document a publisher's declarations align with which EU regulatory concepts. It does NOT certify compliance, does NOT cover every clause, and does NOT replace legal counsel. Operators must consult qualified legal advisors for binding statements.

eu_ai_act_anchors.title: Article 5 - Prohibited AI Practices
eu_ai_act_anchors.scope: All deployers and providers in the EU
a2wf_signals: permissions[].action containing patterns associated with Article 5 categories: remote biometric identification, biometric categorisation by sensitive traits, emotion recognition in workplace or education, social scoring, subliminal techniques, exploitation of vulnerabilities, untargeted facial-image scraping, predictive policing of individuals
eu_ai_act_anchors.guidance: If a permission action name resembles one of the Article 5 categories, the publisher should review whether the practice is actually performed and whether it falls under the prohibitions or one of the narrow exemptions. A2WF declarations alone cannot determine Article 5 applicability; legal review is required.

eu_ai_act_anchors.title: Article 6 - High-Risk AI Systems
eu_ai_act_anchors.scope: Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems in the EU
eu_ai_act_anchors.guidance: Sites in regulated sectors should declare auditTrail and dataHandling modules. Regulated actions should default to handover oversight unless the publisher can document a lawful basis for autonomous handling.

eu_ai_act_anchors.title: Article 13 - Transparency and Provision of Information to Deployers
eu_ai_act_anchors.guidance: A2WF's agentIdentification and discoverabilityHints modules expose machine-readable transparency information. Helpful but not sufficient for Article 13 documentation requirements.

eu_ai_act_anchors.title: Article 14 - Human Oversight
eu_ai_act_anchors.scope: Providers of high-risk AI systems; deployers must respect oversight design
a2wf_signals: oversight.fallback has level handover or confirmation
permissions[].effect in (state-changing, commercial, regulated) AND resolves to oversight.level autonomous
eu_ai_act_anchors.guidance: A2WF's oversight model is a publisher-side declaration of the human-oversight mechanisms available for agent actions. The EU AI Act Article 14 requires EFFECTIVE oversight, not just declared oversight. Publishers should verify that the declared mechanisms actually function.

eu_ai_act_anchors.title: Article 26 - Obligations of Deployers of High-Risk AI Systems
eu_ai_act_anchors.guidance: A2WF's auditTrail-light and incidentReporting modules give deployers a published surface for the record-keeping and incident-handling that Article 26 requires. The modules are declarations; actual record-keeping must happen in the operator's infrastructure.

eu_ai_act_anchors.title: Article 50 - Transparency Obligations for Providers and Deployers
eu_ai_act_anchors.scope: Providers and deployers of certain AI systems
eu_ai_act_anchors.guidance: Sites that interact with natural persons via AI agents may fall under Article 50 transparency. A2WF's agentIdentification module supports the machine-readable side of this transparency.

gdpr_anchors.title: Article 5 - Principles relating to processing of personal data
gdpr_anchors.scope: Any controller processing EU residents' personal data
gdpr_anchors.guidance: Sites processing personal data should declare a dataHandling module with explicit purposes, retention periods, and minimisation flag. A2WF declarations do not satisfy Article 5 by themselves; the controller must actually follow the declared principles.

gdpr_anchors.title: Articles 13-14 - Information to be provided to data subjects
gdpr_anchors.guidance: A2WF's dataHandling module exposes the controller identity and lawful basis as machine-readable declarations. This complements - but does not replace - the human-readable privacy notice required by Articles 13-14.

gdpr_anchors.title: Article 25 - Data protection by design and by default
gdpr_anchors.guidance: Declaring minimisation and conservative oversight is consistent with a data-protection-by-design posture. The declaration is a signal, not proof.

gdpr_anchors.title: Article 33 - Notification of a personal data breach
gdpr_anchors.scope: Controllers in case of a personal data breach
gdpr_anchors.guidance: A2WF's incidentReporting module exposes a machine-readable contact for incident reports. The declared responseTime is the publisher's own intended acknowledgement timeframe and is explicitly NOT a statutory breach-notification deadline (compare GDPR Article 33's 72-hour rule).

readiness_score.description: The A2WF Declaration Coverage Score is a VENDOR METRIC produced by this reference checker. It measures how much of an opinionated baseline of A2WF declarations is present in a document. It is NOT an A2WF conformance metric, NOT a regulatory compliance score, NOT a legal readiness number. The score is capped at 59 on validation failure and at 29 when the validator runs in degraded mode without the JSON Schema bundle. Use it for tracking declaration coverage over time, not for legal claims.

bands.label: High declaration coverage - legal review still required
